assumptions: NCBI's RefSeq assembly annotation, or the Kazusa mirror's table, as served at the time of the fetch.
limits: Counts only annotated CDS; an organism neither source covers cannot be fetched.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: A reader: the codon usage table as the authority publishes it, with nothing inferred; the Codon usage panel's readings are on the tools that use it.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is this organism's codon usage, counted from its annotated CDS or as a published table?

description: Fetch a real codon-usage table for an organism and save it into this project, so later steps can score against it by name. NCBI builds the table by counting codons in the annotated CDS of a RefSeq assembly (the same counting the Codon Usage panel does, with the assembly and CDS count in the provenance); the Kazusa mirror serves a published table for an organism the mirror covers. The table LEAVES NOTHING but takes a network round-trip. Hand the saved name to `codon_usage_analysis` or `codon_optimality` in `table`.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

coverage.description: how much of a multi-replicon assembly to download. `complete` takes every replicon; `budgeted` takes the largest ones that fit a memory budget and SAYS which it used. The panel defaults to complete and falls back when the browser cannot hold the whole thing. Values: complete (Complete assembly), budgeted (Budgeted — largest replicons that fit). Only applies when source is ncbi.

mode.description: which CDS set to count. `heg` uses the highly-expressed-gene set, which is what CAI and Fop reference tables are conventionally built from; `genome` counts every annotated CDS, which describes the organism's average gene rather than its best-expressed one. Values: heg (Highly-expressed genes — the CAI/Fop convention), genome (Whole genome — every annotated CDS). Only applies when source is ncbi.

organism.description: the organism: a scientific name ("Saccharomyces cerevisiae") or an NCBI taxonomy id ("4932"). Resolved live against NCBI — no allow-list (§1 r4) — and the assembly it picks comes back in `report.builtFrom`.

save_as.description: the name to save the table under, as `table` on the other codon tools will spell it. Defaults to the resolved organism plus the basis, which is what the panel names it.

source.description: which register to build the table from. `ncbi` counts the CDS of a RefSeq assembly and covers any organism with one; `kazusa` serves a published table and covers only the organisms its mirror bundles. Values: ncbi (NCBI RefSeq — counted from annotated CDS, any organism), kazusa (Kazusa/CUTG mirror — published table, bundled organisms only).

name: codon_table_fetch

cds.description: how many CDS the table was counted from — the reference-set size, and the number a thin table is thin by. Absent on a register that publishes no counts

codons.description: total codons counted, the weight behind every frequency. ABSENT when the register publishes frequencies rather than counts (the Kazusa mirror does) — never 0, which would be a number you could quote

gc3.description: GC at the third codon position (%), the usage fingerprint. NCBI only; absent elsewhere

organism.description: the organism as the register resolved it, which may be more specific than asked

report.description: the full provenance: register, resolved organism, the identifier the table was built from, and any coverage fallback

table.description: the saved name — wire this straight into `table` on codon_usage_analysis or codon_optimality
